title: Player
summary: Represents a connected person (not their body!): identity (Name, UserId), their Character model, PlayerGui/Backpack containers, leaderstats, and events like CharacterAdded and Chatted.

properties.name: DisplayName
properties.description: The chosen display name (can change, can duplicate — never use as a key).

properties.name: UserId
properties.description: Unique, permanent account ID — the correct key for DataStores and ownership.

properties.name: Character
properties.description: Their current physical body in the world — nil before spawn and briefly during respawn. Respawns create NEW models.

properties.name: Team / TeamColor
properties.description: Team membership when Teams are used.

properties.name: PlayerGui / Backpack / PlayerScripts
properties.description: Per-player containers: live GUIs, tools, client scripts.

events.name: CharacterAdded
events.description: Fires every time a new character spawns. The right place to wire per-character logic.

events.name: CharacterRemoving
events.description: Fires just before the character is removed.

events.name: Chatted
events.description: Server-side: fires when the player sends a chat message.

events.name: Kicked
events.description: Client-side: fires when this client gets kicked.

methods.name: Kick
methods.description: Server: disconnects the player with an optional message.

methods.name: GetJoinData
methods.description: Info about how they joined (launch data, source place).

explanation.whatItIs: The account-side half of a person in your game. The Player sticks around from join to leave; their Character is the physical body that dies and respawns repeatedly.
explanation.whyItExists: Games need a stable identity object (who joined, who owns what, who to save data for) separate from the disposable physical avatar.
whenToUse: Identity & persistence: UserId for DataStore keys
Character lifecycle: CharacterAdded for per-spawn setup
Containers: PlayerGui for runtime UI, Backpack for tools
whenNotToUse: As a physical object — physics happens on Character's parts
DisplayName as a unique key — it's not unique and can change
explanation.mentalModel:
```text
Player (identity, join→leave)
 ├─ UserId: 123456 (forever)
 ├─ Character → Model (dies, respawns, REPLACED)
 ├─ PlayerGui (live UI copies)
 ├─ Backpack (tools)
 └─ leaderstats (Folder → shows on leaderboard)
```
tips: Always handle Character possibly being nil: `local char = player.Character` can be nil between respawns
Wire CharacterAdded in PlayerAdded for complete lifecycle coverage
leaderstats: Folder named exactly 'leaderstats' with NumberValues inside = automatic leaderboard
commonMistakes: Holding a Character reference across respawns — it becomes a dead model; re-fetch on CharacterAdded
Using player.Name as a DataStore key — names can't be guaranteed stable across renames; UserId is forever
Reading Character immediately after PlayerAdded — it may not exist yet; use CharacterAdded or WaitForChild with care

examples.title: Full player lifecycle skeleton
examples.code:
local Players = game:GetService("Players")

local function onCharacterAdded(player, character)
    local humanoid = character:WaitForChild("Humanoid")
    humanoid.Died:Connect(function()
        print(player.Name .. " died; respawning soon")
    end)
end

local function onPlayerAdded(player)
    print(player.Name .. " (" .. player.UserId .. ") joined")

    player.CharacterAdded:Connect(function(character)
        onCharacterAdded(player, character)
    end)
    if player.Character then
        onCharacterAdded(player, player.Character)
    end
end

for _, player in Players:GetPlayers() do
    task.spawn(onPlayerAdded, player)
end
Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(onPlayerAdded)
